The crash in release builds occurred because R8/ProGuard code shrinking is enabled (`isMinifyEnabled = true`), and the default rules (`proguard-android-optimize.txt`) strip the `Signature` bytecode attributes. When Gson's `TypeToken` creates an anonymous class instance at runtime (`object : TypeToken<List<Book>>() {}`), it relies on generic signatures to determine the type arguments; without them, it throws `IllegalStateException`.

### Solution

Added the required rules to [proguard-rules.pro](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c4-agy-B-r4/work/app/proguard-rules.pro):

```proguard
# Preserve generic type signatures and annotations for Gson
-keepattributes Signature
-keepattributes *Annotation*

# Keep Gson's TypeToken and any subclasses/anonymous classes extending it
-keep class com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken { *; }
-keep class * extends com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken
-keepclassmembers class * extends com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken {
    <init>();
}

# Keep data model classes deserialized by Gson
-keep class vn.shelftap.lab.model.** { *; }
```

These rules:
1. Preserve generic type `Signature` attributes across the application so `TypeToken` can resolve the generic type parameters.
2. Prevent R8 from inlining, removing, or stripping type signatures from `TypeToken` and its anonymous subclasses.
3. Keep the model class fields under `vn.shelftap.lab.model` from being renamed or obfuscated during release shrinking so Gson can correctly map JSON fields.
